Firstly Doctor Roberts is an incredible doctor and a lovely lady. She is one in a million. There's also a receptionist who I get on well with and makes me laugh. Last week I saw a bubbly nurse who I thought was superb.

For those of you who have given low marks: If you only get as far as triage and then you are passed onto someone other than a doctor, then it's because spaces are in demand. Pharmacists and nurses are often capable of solving issues BUT if you're still unhappy - then say why and insist on seeing a doctor. The days of everyone getting a free, quick service have ended - so you might as well move with the times - so IF you can afford it, do the rest of us a favour and go private instead of moaning. (Private health insurance doesn't have to cost a fortune).

Now personally, I don't like this modern move towards tech and I use to insist on ringing up. Until I sat and observed just how busy the receptionists actually are and ironically sometimes the result with communicating online can mean you have stuff confirmed in writing rather than on the hoof.

But lets face it, like it or not, everything is being done online and apps now and the NHS isn't going to recover anytime soon (Bevan would be turning in his grave!). Our NHS is broken and serving millions more than it did originally. It's lacked decent investment and wasted millions on middle-management for decades. We have to try utilise other options sometimes to take the pressure off. The system works just as well and for example, when sorting repeat prescriptions, you can see any progress. So try and roll with it if you can.

No surgery is EVER going to be perfect! But let's get this into perspective - I originally went to another in the village - let me very clear here this was NOT John Hampden, this other surgery lost a biopsy (costing me a year of a cancer diagnosis) AND this other surgery also accidentally gave me access to another patients record and then insulted both me and the other lady by trying to cover it up. THAT WOULD NEVER HAPPEN at the John Hampden!

I believe the guys at JH surgery are doing a stirling job, especially given the situation with the country right now. And I for one am very grateful!
